# Static pronunciation data and independent English phonemizer

PageNarrator's phonemizer code is original GPL-3.0-or-later C++/JavaScript. The retained lexical and model metadata below remain third-party data with their own notices and licenses.

| Data | Pinned revision | License |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cmudict/cmudict.dict`, `cmudict.phones` | `cmusphinx/cmudict` `74790861f652b15e4ac49015a90074ad62a27690` | Carnegie Mellon University's permissive redistribution license; retain `cmudict/LICENSE` |
| `ipa-dict/data/en_UK.txt` | `open-dict-data/ipa-dict` `43c3570eb3553bdd19fccd2bd0091534889af023` | GPL-3.0 for this dataset, conservatively treated as GPL-3.0-only; retain `ipa-dict/GPL-3.0.txt` |
| `kokoro-tokenizer*.json`, vocabulary metadata | `onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX` `1939ad2a8e416c0acfeecc08a694d14ef25f2231` | Apache-2.0 model metadata; retain the Kokoro/model notices |

The UK data's original attribution is **ipacards**, Melissa Boiko (published under the former account/name `leoboiko`/Leonardo Boiko), with eSpeak-generated lexical transcriptions. See the upstream [dataset credits](https://github.com/open-dict-data/ipa-dict/tree/43c3570eb3553bdd19fccd2bd0091534889af023#credits), retained `ipa-dict/README.upstream.md`, and [ipacards' generation credits](https://github.com/melissaboiko/ipacards/blob/master/deck_description.md). The repository-wide MIT label on ipa-dict does not replace this UK dataset's GPL license. These are fixed word/pronunciation records, not an eSpeak rule program. No `en_rules`, compiled `en_dict`, phoneme bytecode, language instruction tables, or upstream phonemizer runtime is used by this implementation.

`sources.json` pins every downloaded lexical source by immutable URL, byte count and SHA-256. Run `node scripts/build-pronunciation-data.mjs --download` to retrieve those sources and compile the data; later builds need no network. `--check` reconstructs the same bytes and checks the converter/source identities. Kokoro's raw character tokenizer fixtures are retained for small portable contract tests, not a third-party tokenizer implementation.

The original converter reads literal lexical records, normalizes spelling case/diacritics, preserves distinct pronunciation alternatives, converts CMU ARPABET explicitly, and validates every retained phone against the pinned Kokoro vocabulary. The `PNPRON01` binary contains sorted words, bounded alternatives and character IDs only. Its C++ reader validates sections, ordering, lengths and record bounds before binary lookup. `excluded.json` records each omitted source word, source and reason; the generated `pronunciations.json` summarizes classifications. Ordinary builds can verify source/binary agreement without downloading or running upstream code.

Current data contains 125,112 US words, 65,118 UK words and 199,254 pronunciation variants. There are 1,029 excluded source records: 1,013 CMU punctuation/non-word records, 15 CMU leading-apostrophe records, and the UK entry `llanos` containing /ɬ/, which Kokoro's vocabulary cannot encode. Original normalization expands four common leading-apostrophe colloquialisms; others proceed through ordinary word segmentation. No unsupported phone is silently dropped. The plain uppercase UK entry `I` is normalized to the lookup key `i`.

`native/phonemizer.cpp` contains the independent lexical reader and original bounded English OOV spelling rules. Build with Zig 0.15.2 via `PN_ZIG=... node scripts/build-browser-phonemizer.mjs`; `--check` verifies the checked-in source/WASM/flags without needing a compiler. The compiled module has no runtime imports and a 32 MiB memory ceiling. JavaScript uses browser Unicode APIs for text normalization and releases the native instance on disposal.

Lookup order is contextual overrides, dialect lexicon, known-stem inflection, known compound pieces, original OOV spelling rules, then letter-name spelling for residual tokens. Clause punctuation is retained for Kokoro; raw source text is retained by the streaming adapter. Full batch synthesis concatenates all bounded segments instead of silently truncating phoneme IDs.

The registry uses this implementation through its packaged worker and inference engine. Its original OOV stress/spelling rules are approximate, the UK dictionary omits some heteronyms, and word-level records cannot reproduce all of eSpeak's sentence-level pronunciation decisions. Frozen contextual pronunciation, source association, long Heart/Emma listening and real worker/cache lifecycle checks cover their recorded cases. Unit/native/kernel parity does not establish broader pronunciation quality. Physical-tier throughput and broad pronunciation remain unverified. No exact eSpeak parity or general speech speedup is claimed. See [release status](../../docs/release-readiness.md).

`node scripts/probe-english-pronunciation.mjs --regression` independently associates every compiled variant with its declared raw source and checks every native lookup, including alternatives and excluded-record attribution. The original manual pronunciation fixture exposed voiced-final-s and consonant-le gaps; those cases now serve as regression data. Its four strict UK final-vowel differences (`ɐ` in retained records versus manual `ə`) remain strict gold failures. `acceptance-classifications.json` associates each with its exact retained citation form and documented British lowered final-COMMA variation; it neither rewrites gold nor equates all `ɐ`/`ə` contexts. Fixed lexical variants do not prove connected-speech allophony or a model's acoustic realization.

The original bounded context cues select common `read`, `record`, and `close` variants using nearby auxiliaries, determiners, tense adverbs and punctuation boundaries. They are not a general part-of-speech parser. Original OOV rules distinguish a later unstressed `-er/-ers` from a stressed single-syllable r-colored vowel. `scripts/probe-english-contextual.mjs` preserves first frozen sentence evaluations separately from later regressions and records all source/data pins; `--corpus v3` selects the fresh follow-up. Small-corpus passes do not qualify all English pronunciation.

The fixed six-case narration corpus in `tests/fixtures/kokoro-semantic-corpus.json` covers US/UK voices, speeds and finite streaming. Run `scripts/probe-kokoro-semantics.mjs --cache <verified-model-directory>` for the original WASM/q8 path, or add `--webgpu` for original WebGPU/f32. Optional `--asr-model <existing-pinned-Whisper-snapshot>` uses the development-only offline ASR oracle and writes paired WAVs and `review.html`. Reports retain separate functional, ASR and strict waveform outcomes; an ASR pass does not establish naturalness or human listening acceptance. GPU runs require an exclusive hardware slot. Development intervention probes may supply reference intermediates solely to diagnose drift; the production loader never uses those substitutions or the reference inference runtime.
